entities.summary: Craig Patrick is an American former hockey player, coach and general manager, the son of Lynn Patrick and the grandson of Lester Patrick. During the 1980 Winter Olympics, Patrick was the assistant general manager and assistant coach under Herb Brooks for the United States men's national ice hockey team, which won the gold medal and defeated the Soviet Union in the "Miracle on Ice". From 1989 to 2006, Patrick was the general manager of the Pittsburgh Penguins where he oversaw back-to-back Stanley Cup championships in 1991 and 1992, as well as the drafting and signing of some players that would later win a Stanley Cup title for the Penguins in 2009.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Craig Patrick's role as assistant general manager and coach of the US men's national ice hockey team at the 1980 Winter Olympics led to a gold medal victory over the Soviet Union, marking a significant moment in American sports history. His later success as GM of the Pittsburgh Penguins contributed to back-to-back Stanley Cup championships.
